raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
`Dockerfile.rock_base` cherry-picks [ROCm/rocm-systems#12089](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/12089) so the ROCm 10 wheel's rocprofiler-sdk no longer bus-locks while the torch profiler reuses HSA signals. Fixes #61896.

## Overview

Replace `librocprofiler-sdk.so.1` with a build of `ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT` plus `86dd3bab5b`, until the ROCm 10 wheel contains that commit.

## Claims

- On one MI350X, ROCm 7.2.3 has no idle after kernel 7. The ROCm 10 hole drops by about 2–4× after the library swap. With the profiler on, a 2048-kernel replay goes from 7.50 ms to 7.09 ms, against 6.87 ms on ROCm 7.2.3. The kernel-7 idle is 13% of the profiler-on gap before the swap and 4–5% after.
- Stock `pool<signal_t>::m_buffer` at `0xba7514` is 4-byte aligned; the rebuilt library aligns it so `m_reused` stays inside one cache line.

## Validation

`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`. The two stock columns are the nightlies built from the same vLLM commit, `3f1bcfd82bb2e93fcd364fc7a5491718453a77e2`: ROCm 7.2.3 `nightly-3f1bcfd82bb2e93fcd364fc7a5491718453a77e2` and ROCm 10 `nightly-rocm100-3f1bcfd82bb2e93fcd364fc7a5491718453a77e2`.

Overlay is an older ROCm 10 nightly, `nightly-rocm100-36768d1bfd39094681cdbc8cb37d4b31c0729c89`, not a vLLM rebuild: only the real `librocprofiler-sdk.so.1` is replaced with rocprofiler-sdk built from `ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT` plus `86dd3bab5b`. Everything else in that image stays the nightly bits. This PR is that same replacement inside `docker build -f docker/Dockerfile.rock_base --target final`. Probe is in #61896.

Idle after kernel 7 of each of two replays:

| N | ROCm 7.2.3 | ROCm 10 | ROCm 10 overlay | This PR |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 256 | ~0 µs | 56 µs, 482 µs | 69 µs, 84 µs | 48 µs, 53 µs |
| 512 | ~0 µs | 517 µs, 591 µs | 157 µs, 182 µs | 157 µs, 136 µs |
| 2048 | ~0 µs | 540 µs, 523 µs | 116 µs, 164 µs | 142 µs, 175 µs |

One replay, median of 7. Wall time is `profiler off→on (+overhead)`. Idle share is shown as `7.2 / 10.0 / PR`; it is approximate because wall time and idle come from different replays.

| N | ROCm 7.2 wall (ms) | ROCm 10.0 wall (ms) | This PR wall (ms) | Idle share: 7.2 / 10.0 / PR |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 256 | 0.43→0.88 (+105%) | 0.43→1.43 (+233%) | 0.43→1.07 (+149%) | ~0 / 6–48% / 8% |
| 512 | 0.85→1.73 (+104%) | 0.86→2.27 (+164%) | 0.85→1.93 (+127%) | ~0 / 37–42% / 13–15% |
| 2048 | 3.36→6.87 (+104%) | 3.39→7.50 (+121%) | 3.37→7.09 (+110%) | ~0 / 13% / 4–5% |

Most profiler overhead is present on ROCm 7.2.3 too. At N=2048 the raw ROCm 10 idle is 13% of that overhead; after this PR it is 4–5%.

CI does not build this base image. The run above is the check.

## Details

`static_object` placement-new'd `pool<signal_t>` into an unaligned byte buffer ([ROCm/rocm-systems#9639](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/issues/9639)). `m_reused` is `lock incq 0xe8(pool)`. At `mod 64 = 20` that atomic starts at byte 60 and crosses the cache line. The increment runs once a profiled kernel reuses a signal, which is the second graph replay. The core/devel symlink for the rocprofiler SONAMEs stays; the new file is installed on the devel copy those links follow. Drop the stage when the wheel ships ROCm/rocm-systems#12089.

---

@Rohan138 @okorzh-amd 
Thanks for the comments! I just created a new committ so the change is applied to the right file.
From what I gathered [rocm-systems#12089](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/12089) did not make it to ROCm 10.1. Because by the time 12089 got merged into devel branch, 10.1 was cut before that point. So, I believe regardless of the upgrade to 10.1 or any change in `ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT`, the cherry picking should work.
Since this PR doesn't touch `ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT` I would leave that for other PR to decide its fait :)

Just a followup comment for clarification. [PR#62536](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62536) by @rasmith attempting to bump to ROCm 10.1 does not have this fix in the rocm-system commit path.
But it improves the profiler footprint issue. At least the profiler bugfix here doesn't have any effect on the probe when ROCm 10.1 lands. but it is possible that the probe script is not the best representation. I am working on testing @rasmith's image on KimiK3 that initially manifested the issue. For reference the probe script and two PRs look like below:

| N | ROCm 7.2.3 | ROCm 10 stock | #61887 | #62536 | #62536 + #61887 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 256 | +105% | +233% | +149% | +139% | +139% |
| 512 | +104% | +164% | +127% | +121% | +127% |
| 2048 | +104% | +121% | +110% | +110% | +110% |

(lower better = effect of profiler on duration of graph)
`ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT` `4baa067` does not contain `86dd3bab` (rocm-systems#12089) but eliminates its effect somehow :)

I collected traces for KimiK3 using the future docker image in [#62536](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62536) with/without this rocprof fix; there is no visible differences in traces anymore. 
So, I am closing this. As I mentioned in previous comment, although the new ROCm 10.1 doesn't have this specific librocprofiler-sdk version there is also no visible benefit in this specific version of the rocprofiler.

files.patch:
@@ -14,6 +14,8 @@ ARG MORI_BRANCH="v1.2.3.post1"
 ARG MORI_REPO="https://github.com/ROCm/mori.git"
 ARG ROCM_SYSTEMS_REPO="https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems.git"
 ARG ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT="25e14349f2606a6b95c4ccd45eb92a1835646cf2"
+# Drop once the ROCm 10 wheel contains ROCm/rocm-systems#12089.
+ARG ROCPROFILER_SDK_FIX_COMMIT="86dd3bab5b9f8c360a2c2dcc13d6238cb3cdce2b"
 
 
 # TheRock configuration
@@ -326,6 +328,41 @@ RUN mkdir -p /staging/lib \
     && ls -l /staging/lib
 
 
+###
+### rocprofiler-sdk split-lock fix
+###
+# The 10.0 wheel places static_object storage below alignof(Tp). pool<signal_t>
+# then bus-locks on m_reused while the torch profiler reuses HSA signals.
+FROM base AS build_rocprofiler_sdk
+ARG ROCM_SYSTEMS_REPO
+ARG ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT
+ARG ROCPROFILER_SDK_FIX_COMMIT
+SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c"]
+RUN apt-get update \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends g++ libdw-dev libelf-dev libdrm-dev libsqlite3-dev xxd \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+RUN git clone -q --filter=blob:none --no-checkout ${ROCM_SYSTEMS_REPO} /src && cd /src \
+    && git sparse-checkout init --cone \
+    && git sparse-checkout set projects/rocprofiler-sdk shared cmake \
+    && git checkout -q ${ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT} \
+    && git -c user.email=x@x -c user.name=x cherry-pick -n ${ROCPROFILER_SDK_FIX_COMMIT} \
+    && grep -q "alignas" projects/rocprofiler-sdk/source/lib/common/static_object.hpp \
+    && git submodule update --init --depth 1 --jobs 8 -- projects/rocprofiler-sdk/external
+ENV SYSDEPS="$SDK_DEV/lib/rocm_sysdeps"
+RUN cd /src/projects/rocprofiler-sdk \
+    && cmake -B build -G Ninja \
+        -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
+        -DROCPROFILER_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \
+        -DROCPROFILER_BUILD_SAMPLES=OFF \
+        -DROCPROFILER_BUILD_DOCS=OFF \
+        -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$SDK_DEV;$SYSDEPS" \
+        -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/rp-install \
+    && cmake --build build --parallel 16 --target rocprofiler-sdk-shared-library \
+    && mkdir -p /staging \
+    && cp "$(readlink -f "$(find build -name 'librocprofiler-sdk.so.1*' -type f | head -1)")" /staging/librocprofiler-sdk.so.fixed \
+    && ls -la /staging
+
+
 ###
 ### Final Build
 ###
@@ -400,6 +437,19 @@ RUN set -eux; \
 
 RUN ldconfig
 
+COPY --from=build_rocprofiler_sdk /staging/librocprofiler-sdk.so.fixed /tmp/librocprofiler-sdk.so.fixed
+# Symlinks keep their targets; only the real SONAME file is replaced.
+RUN set -eux; \
+    replaced=0; \
+    for f in "$SDK_DEV"/lib/librocprofiler-sdk.so.1* "$SDK_CORE"/lib/librocprofiler-sdk.so.1*; do \
+        [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue; \
+        install -m 0644 /tmp/librocprofiler-sdk.so.fixed "$f"; \
+        replaced=$((replaced + 1)); \
+    done; \
+    test "$replaced" -ge 1; \
+    rm -f /tmp/librocprofiler-sdk.so.fixed; \
+    ldconfig
+
 # This is to prevent resolvers from checking METADATA and RECORD and clobbering
 # the Triton source build we installed. Constraints files are unable to help
 # with this. However, these entries are optional and can be blanked which
@@ -442,6 +492,7 @@ ARG MORI_BRANCH
 ARG MORI_REPO
 ARG ROCM_SYSTEMS_REPO
 ARG ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT
+ARG ROCPROFILER_SDK_FIX_COMMIT
 ARG TRITON_VERSION
 # Record hashes for Triton and pybind11 so we can verify later.
 RUN echo "BASE_IMAGE: ${BASE_IMAGE}" > /app/versions.txt \
@@ -462,6 +513,7 @@ RUN echo "BASE_IMAGE: ${BASE_IMAGE}" > /app/versions.txt \
     && echo "MORI_REPO: ${MORI_REPO}" >> /app/versions.txt \
     && echo "ROCM_SYSTEMS_REPO: ${ROCM_SYSTEMS_REPO}" >> /app/versions.txt \
     && echo "ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT: ${ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT}" >> /app/versions.txt \
+    && echo "ROCPROFILER_SDK_FIX_COMMIT: ${ROCPROFILER_SDK_FIX_COMMIT}" >> /app/versions.txt \
     # Fingerprint our triton so Dockerfile.rocm can prove it survived the build.
     && echo "TRITON_VERSION: $(pip show triton | awk '/^Version:/ {print $2}')" >> /app/versions.txt \
     && echo "TRITON_SHA256: $(find $(python3 -c 'import triton, os; print(os.path.dirname(triton.__file__))') \
